quest.title: Ancient Shadows Re-Emerge
quest.description: The Jinn-induced sandstorm has subsided. Return to the Temple of Silence and discuss the situation with your friends.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IX
chapter.title: As All Falls to Emptiness

dialogues.speaker: Kashif
dialogues.text: Let's not tell Madam Faruzan about Miss Nicole's true identity for now...

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Good idea. Let's limit the conversation to aesthetics...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So this is the Temple of Silence... I've heard the Nagarjunites mention it in passing, but I never imagined it would be this big. It's colossal...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I thought the Temple moved to the rainforest ages ago? When did they scamper back into the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Rushd
dialogues.text: ...I don't know, this plan sounds a little too risky for my liking.

dialogues.speaker: Shakir
dialogues.text: Even in King Deshret's day, this was experimental technology. We have no idea what could happen if we activate it.

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: Well, unless you know of another viable alternative for the Akasha Terminal, I'm afraid this is our only option.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: The plan is sound, and the risks are manageable. However, if we are to proceed, we must act quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: The scale of this project is enormous. Even with Kaveh, Faruzan, and every other scholar of mechanics working on it full time, the proposed modifications won't happen overnight...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're back... Everything alright?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Uh... And who are they?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Friends of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, pretty much everyone in the Temple of Silence is! This guy's Kaveh, and the one next to him is Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hello. I'm Jeht, and this is Liloupar.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Oh? A famous name from the history books.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Pleased to meet you. A friend of a friend is a friend of mine, as they say!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Who's "they"?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? ...Do people not say that?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Not in the desert. Friends you can trust, but friends of friends? Gotta keep an eye on them.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Still, I do trust {NICKNAME}'s judgment. I'm sure you're good people.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The sandstorms have calmed down. I take it the Gurabad problem is resolved? What did you find?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell everyone what happened in Gurabad...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And after getting all smarmy with us, he trapped us there. Luckily, Jeht used the mechanism outside to free us, and then we got Liloupar to put a stop to the chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wow... Thanks for being there to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So. This mystery man openly admitted that he was merely a Harbinger's subordinate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Is there something weird about that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Now that he mentions it, it is a little strange...)
Hehe... I assume you aren't naive enough to expect answers from an enemy?
Well deduced. Our commander, Dottore, died in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (He was clearly unwilling to answer our questions when we first met, so why would he admit to being Dottore's subordinate later?)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Are you wondering about his true identity? Or do you think there's a big conspiracy behind all this?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I wouldn't go as far as to call it a conspiracy. Just the simple fact that having someone to shift the blame on tends to prove useful, should trouble come knocking later.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The most important thing for now is to solve the immediate problem. Perhaps that man knew you wouldn't have the resources to investigate his background, and so didn't put much effort into disguising himself.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Uhh... This is all getting a little cryptic for me. I'll let you guys talk while I take a walk with Liloupar.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Aren't you with the Blazing Beasts? What a coincidence. Didn't expect to run into you here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Eh, we're mercs, you can run into us anywhere. Who's this with you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, did you find the solution you were looking for in the Temple of Silence?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You bet we did. This place is incredible — it has everything.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So far, we've discussed a plan and verified its feasibility. Building a new system from scratch is out of the question, so our only option is to modify the Akasha using certain resources we hope to find in the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: According to certain sources in the Temple of Silence, there is a core device in King Deshret's Mausoleum known as "Aaru." Little is known about this device in academic circles, which suggests it was hidden quite effectively.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: If these sources prove correct, the energy contained within Aaru may be sufficient to power our Akasha renovation plan.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: However, this raises difficult questions regarding technological integration. The sages are still debating it.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Yeah, but I'm sure they'll reach a compromise once they've argued it out.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: The people of the rainforest are always cautious when it comes to desert technology, but times of crisis like this leave us with little choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait. Paimon has a question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this the same Aaru we've heard of before? It's sealed off, right? Some sort of prison where the Goat King, Ibis King, and Crocodile King are locked up.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Well remembered. Yes, that's exactly right.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: According to our records, Aaru was the most brilliant creation King Deshret ever conceived of. Built by divine and mortal artisans working together, it was a miraculous accomplishment, and it lies hidden deep within the king's Mausoleum to this day.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: That being said, what Aaru actually does and why it was built... Those are deep secrets we are not privy to.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Until recently, I wouldn't have been optimistic that the place even exists. The only reason I'm inclined to believe it now is because we heard it from the Ibis King Thoth himself at his temple... The tale of how the three retainers of Al-Ahmar were imprisoned in Aaru.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon totally gets that. When Paimon first heard about it, she thought it sounded pretty unbelievable, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you guys still remember that? The Ibis King told us they were trapped in Aaru, and that they had to answer three questions to get out.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: I think I remember... "What causes our rise and fall," "what obliterates love and hate," and "what determines truth and falsehood"... those were the three questions, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. If only Nefer were here... She's dealt with the Ibis King before, so she might know more... Oh — Nefer's a friend we met in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: ...Nod-Krai? Huh, funny. She showed up here earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Yeah. Had another lady with her, too. Both said they knew you. They contacted the sages, claiming they might be able to offer some assistance.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Really? They came here to help out?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Yes, really. It was just before you got back.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: One of them said she's made Nod-Krai her home. If she's the person you were talking about, then...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Looks like betting on Aaru was the right choice.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: See? They're right over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nicole, Nefer!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Why, hello. We're here to help!

talks.objective: Talk to your two old friends

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It's a good thing we left early. We almost got locked out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Locked out? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, you haven't heard? An invisible barrier has appeared around Sumeru's borders, cutting off all travel in and out.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: No one can leave and no one can enter. Sumeru has become a lonely island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are the Fatui behind this too?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Actually, no. This has nothing to do with them. I suspect it's a defense mechanism within Irminsul itself.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Irminsul is the source of Teyvat's Ley Lines, after all, and Sumeru is the nation closest to it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I imagine this function was put in place to seal the entire region off in the event of serious damage, preventing the disaster from spreading to the rest of Teyvat. It may have been implemented long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But doesn't that mean that the people here won't be able to escape to other nations if the anomaly keeps spreading?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Currently, that does appear to be the case. Which is precisely why I am here. This is a critical moment for the world, and Sumeru is the eye of the storm.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you brought Nefer here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's surprised you managed to convince her to come back to Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Indeed... Even for someone of my wisdom and eloquence, this tested my skills to the limit...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...And why should it concern me that Sumeru's in trouble? Surely you don't think I still have feelings for that place?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Judging by your tone, I suppose you don't.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sounds like you don't know much about my past. And here I thought you knew everything.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: All I know is that the Ibis King is the source of your power. He was quite a prominent Moon Envoy once upon a time... so I do know a thing or two about him.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: As for your past, I have ways to learn the full story if I wished to. But everyone has secrets they'd rather keep to themselves, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm glad you see it that way, Miss Nicole.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I've chosen to call Nod-Krai home, which is why I did my part in its hour of need. That doesn't mean world-saving's become a habit with me. I have no particular desire to play hero in Sumeru, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I understand. Human emotions do not appear and disappear without cause. There is always a reason to be found behind both salvation and destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Still, if time has taught me anything, it's that human emotions are often complex and in conflict. That's why people change their minds about things all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But that's where we angels come in. Our duty, ultimately, is to guide people towards their deepest, truest desires, and help bring them to fruition.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So I wish to hear about your past. Because I do not believe you are motivated by hatred alone. And if we still arrive at different conclusions in the end, that's okay.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I refuse.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Wait, what? But I set the atmosphere and everything... Isn't this supposed to be the moment when we finally open up to one another?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Is it? Maybe I'm not so good at reading the atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...You're right, Nicole. There's more to me than just hatred. Had it consumed me, I'd be left stuck in the past forever, never living in the present.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But I don't think that your guidance can change my mind. The all-consuming sands, the bloodshed both deserved and undeserved... Those old emotions cling to me like a shadow.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Do you wish to shake them off?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...No, I hope to remember them forever. Those emotions and memories shaped me into the person I am today. They'll always be a part of me.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm... In that case, would you like to hear my perspective, at least?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Sure. It's not every day you get to hear an angel's opinion.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: A long, long time ago, when the angels still walked freely upon the earth, I found life tedious.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Monotonous work, lukewarm relationships... Things weren't nearly as interesting as they are now. And yet, since the angels' demise, I have found myself missing those days on more than one occasion...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Human emotions are often attached to a person, a place, or an object. When those things are gone, the memories quickly fade, and the emotions slip away along with them.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If Sumeru were destroyed, both rainforest and desert would be no more. With the object of your hatred wiped from existence, it would not take long for the memories buried deep in your heart to slowly fade.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Both love and hate are intense emotions. But they are nothing compared to the void left behind when they disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Most sophisticated, Miss Nicole. But anyone focused on the future could only ever applaud the destruction of the things they hate.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Still... I'm a special case. Someone once told me that human memory is more selective than a Mora-hungry merchant choosing between customers. We all need a reality check once in a while, so we don't forget the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As much as I dislike Sumeru, this is no way for it to perish... Alright, you win. I'll help you out a little, but I won't work for free.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: How much will you need? You're not going to milk this for all it's worth, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Uh... I'll be upfront with you — I don't have much Mora on me. If that's what you need, I could borrow some from Alice... Or perhaps I could pay in sculptures? The ones I carve are actually worth quite a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Just cover my travel expenses.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that all?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That's all.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Given all the people I owe favors to, I can just about justify a trip to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Jahoda!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Here, Boss. What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm going back to Sumeru for a while. While I'm away, you'll be in charge of the Curatorium.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wh... M—Me? I—I'm in charge? Whoa... Ahem! Don't worry, Boss! You can count on me!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And that was how the ingenious angel Nicole brought you the perfect person for the job in your hour of need. Hip, hip, hooray!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That was far more detailed than necessary. Not lacking in embellishment, either.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I never thought I'd return, especially not the desert. But life doesn't always go as planned, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What's Candace up to? I don't think I've seen her yet.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: She's still taking care of things in Aaru Village. Should be joining us before too long.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Oh, and sorry, hope we're not interrupting anything. We have some good news, though.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We're planning to go to the Mausoleum of King Deshret to look for the legendary Aaru, then use it to try and restore the Akasha System.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: According to records in the Temple of Silence, the mausoleum houses something called "Aaru's Shut," which can be used to establish connection with Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We still have some time before we leave, so there's no rush.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: By the way, who are these two new faces?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Just call me Nefer. I'm based in Nod-Krai. Did I hear you mention Aaru?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, I happen to have a connection with one of the three retainers imprisoned inside, the Ibis King. I'm here to get things done, so if you don't mind, I think I should come with you.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That sounds perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm... Miss Nefer, are you from the desert by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Why do you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I dunno. There's a familiar air about you, plus you mentioned Candace... Sorry, I don't mean to pry. It was just a random thought.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm Dehya, an Eremite mercenary. My work usually keeps me out in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm on good terms with Dori, and she's mentioned you all before. It's nice to finally put faces to the names.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: However, my associate here is probably less well acquainted with you. Why don't you all introduce yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Actually, I'm a little better acquainted than you might think.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh. Are my eyes playing tricks on me? It looked like you spoke without moving your mouth...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ventriloquism... I have heard tell of it before.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What is it, Collei?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's you... You're the voice who's been speaking in my head, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You encouraged me to report my dreams to the Dendro Archon, and got me to recite that magic prayer...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. I have many titles, but let's go with the most pertinent one. I am Nicole Reeyn, an angel who has lived since ancient times.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: An angel? Sounds like a big deal... But, uh, what exactly is an angel?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, hmm... Well, we're a rather long-living race of beings. Not gods, technically, but we can still tell you a lot of stories from ancient history.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, and she's also an amazing sculptor!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could say she's a real creative type.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Haha... Well, Ma'am, if both {NICKNAME} and Paimon give you rave reviews, you must be pretty impressive!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, please don't call me "Ma'am." I find it so awkward when people get too formal with me.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Just relax and be yourselves. No need to be nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole, if it's okay... could I ask you a few questions?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes, you may. I can see your heart is filled with confusion, and you are desperate for answers.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I also know which questions you want to ask me. Why did you dream of Sumeru City in disarray? Why did those verses soothe the Jinn only when recited by you?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I can guide you to the truth, but it involves a personal secret of yours. I'd prefer to speak with you alone if possible.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I thought we were going to speak alone... This is a lot more people than I was expecting.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's wrong with it? Even the doctors at Bimarstan allow patients to be accompanied by family members.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, if Collei doesn't mind her secret being revealed, I have no problem with it.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thanks for being so considerate, Miss Nicole. I don't know what secret you mean, but whatever it is, there's no need for me to hide it from my closest friends.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Closest friends! Ah, it's so nice to hear that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here to support Collei through this.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alright. In that case, I'll get right to it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Collei, are you aware that there are god remains inside your body?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...I am.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: When I was young, I got sick with Eleazar. Nothing could cure it.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: The Fatui convinced my mom and dad that they could help, and I was sent to an unfamiliar place.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: There were a lot of other kids just like me there. This creepy guy injected us with some strange medicine... which I heard contained god remains.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I can still remember the pain like it was yesterday. But thanks to the friends who've stuck by me all this time, I've gradually been able to overcome those memories.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Anyway... So you're saying that what happened to me has something to do with the god remains they injected me with?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes. Those were the remains of Nabu Malikata... the Goddess of Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh, Cyno & Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh, Cyno & Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh, Cyno & Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Huh... Fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You don't seem surprised like the rest of us. Why?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The possibility crossed my mind when Collei recited the Goddess of Flowers' song and calmed the Jinn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah! You made Paimon jump! What are you doing here, Liloupar?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I was merely passing through, when I heard the name of the Goddess of Flowers. Be assured that I share your surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: You with the hat — are you certain? I sense no trace of the Lord of Flowers within her.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, it is a very small fragment. Unless special {RUBY#[D]poems and prayers}methods are used to manifest its power, even her closest acquaintances would find it near impossible to detect.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: After the Goddess passed away, her remains were scattered across the desert. King Deshret gathered all the pieces he could find and buried them in the Eternal Oasis, but some fragments remained unaccounted for.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Eventually, the Fatui must have found a way to track some of them down... Presumably for use in some experiment. It's not an uncommon occurrence.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm. You're more shaken than I thought. In one sense, you've been extraordinarily lucky. So many people who yearn for this kind of power never attain it, yet you have coexisted with her all this time without even realizing it.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't know what to say. I'm glad that I could help everyone with this power, really. But knowing that a fragment of the Goddess of Flowers is inside my body is... It's a strange feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, people value their autonomy very highly. Even a well-intentioned intruder can shake one's sense of self.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I understand how you feel, Collei. But once you get used to it, you'll find it's nothing to be concerned about.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh... I guess you of all people have a good reason to speak on this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Two good reasons, in fact. Incidentally, three is the maximum number of Hermanubis's Ba fragments that I could bear.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let me guess, because two's company but three's a crowd?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hehe... Thanks for helping to explain the joke, Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Not my intention!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Goddess preserve me, I should take my leave. This boy in his wolf's-head hat speaks much too differently from the Hermanubis I remember.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei, all I'm trying to say is, no matter how many Hermanubis fragments there are within me, you wouldn't think of me as Hermanubis. In the same way, you are simply you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah, I know what you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So about that dream I had... Was it a warning from the Goddess of Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes. Just like me, she was an angel created by the primordial humans, born with the instinct to guide living beings.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Though her body and soul have perished, her essence retains its natural instincts. Even her smallest remaining fragments would do their utmost to send you that warning.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The Mother of Dreams, Lord of Flowers and Oases... She must have had a premonition. That is why she gave that dream to you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I... We won't let her efforts go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But I still don't understand... Why me?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes, why indeed? You weren't the only one injected with god remains, but only in you have her fragments persisted.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I suspect it may be because of the firm will you showed in the face of suffering. She was likely assimilated by that will.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Of course, this doesn't mean you have to shoulder any extra responsibility. As this young man said — you are who you are, and that will not change.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alright, any further questions from the "family members of the patient"? If not, we should head to the Mausoleum of King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's move out. Time to put our plan into action.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: We all hope it'll work... But will we really be able to open Aaru? And even if all seven pillars of King Deshret agree to let us proceed, the scale of the work to follow is daunting to say the least...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Haven't you handled other big projects before?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I mean, the biggest project I've worked on to date is probably... the Palace of Alcazarzaray, I guess? But this is orders of magnitude beyond that. It's a total nightmare.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Look on the bright side. At least this time, you're actually here when Sumeru needs you most. You won't have to come asking me for details after the fact.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph, mock me all you want! But now that I'm here, things will be resolved far more quickly and smoothly than last time!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Kaveh's self-doubt disappeared in an instant... Like magic.)

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, this confidence is most gladdening. Now, go and pack your things. We'll head to the Mausoleum as soon as you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Oh, Miss Nicole! I heard you're a very talented sculptor. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, I don't know... I wouldn't want to blow my own trumpet...

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Honestly, even though Kshahrewar is best known for its focus on mechanics, plenty of Kshahrewar scholars are quite serious about sculpting as a hobby.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: So if they rate your work, that's enough for us! We just have to take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Who's "we"?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Myself and a few other scholars. Kashif, Daneshvar, come take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, if you insist, I... I suppose there's no harm in showing you...

dialogues.speaker: Kashif
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did that come from?

dialogues.speaker: Daneshvar
dialogues.text: Look at the level of detail. It's so lifelike...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The squirrel descends from the heavens like a champion, and the earth trembles beneath its feet. What do you think? Striking, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Kaveh? Ah, Kaveh! Come here for a sec. Oh, and Madam Faruzan, didn't you use to study in our Darshan? Come take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, but hang on a moment! I have to finish reviewing this proposal first!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmm? You called? What is it, youngster?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: This squirrel statue. Isn't it cute?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh? A squirrel... I wouldn't say "cute," per se. The realism is what stands out to me. Were you trying to carve a statue of a hero, young lady?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: A hero? I suppose so... Actually, I didn't really have a specific theme in mind. I just started working on it, and this is how it turned out.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I see. Well, do you tend to read novels about heroes in your spare time?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: As a matter of fact, I do quite enjoy those. Everyone loves a good tale of derring-do, right?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Then perhaps this statue represents the heroic tale you long to see deep down inside.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Also, on the subject of heroism... I feel that if the subject posed with a finger raised towards the heavens, it would lend a greater gravitas to the overall image.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'm sure some would call it cliché or old-fashioned, but not me — I think it would be a perfect fit. It has a certain classical beauty about it.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Kaveh! Kaveh!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Sorry, Madam Faruzan, I'm a little busy right now. Don't wait up for me!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: What a pity. That young man has excellent aesthetic tastes, I was hoping to ask him for his opinion.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: What a genius idea! Why didn't I think of that? Classical beauty is a great direction to explore... That's it, once I get back, I'm going to sculpt a heroic squirrel pointing its finger towards the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Precisely! A declaration of victory! You understand my vision.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Then, place the two statues face-to-face...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes! That's exactly what I was thinking!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: It'll be a masterpiece! Miss.... I'm sorry, I didn't catch your name?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Just call me Nicole. Um... M—Madam Faruzan, was it?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: What? No, no, no, that wouldn't be right...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Whyever not? "Madam" is a state of mind, cultivated from within. Anyone may call me "Madam" if they so desire.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: My dear Miss Nicole, once we make it through these trying times, should we have the pleasure of meeting again, I shall look forward to seeing your new work.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: In this day and age, it's rare to find people with an appreciation for classical aesthetics. Meeting you was truly a pleasant surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Honestly, I feel the same way. It's been a long time since I met anyone interested in this style of statue. Clearly, they don't call you "Madam" for nothing!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Also, I have to say, you're a very good judge of character... Because when I think about it, I really am someone who likes stories about heroes. That must be why I've quietly kept watch over generation after generation of them.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Sorry? Keeping watch over heroes? Um... What exactly do you do for a living...?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Never mind that.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Let's not tell Madam Faruzan about Miss Nicole's true identity for now...

dialogues.speaker: Kashif
dialogues.text: Good idea. Let's limit the conversation to aesthetics...

talks.objective: Go to the Great Hall of Truths
Go deeper into the Great Hall of Truths

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why, we've not seen so many visitors... ever, really. What is this place now, a tourist attraction?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah. Closer inspection reveals many familiar faces. To what do we dusty old fellows owe the honor? Surely you're not just here to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You surmise correctly. We are here to carry out a rather enormous project.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hoho, enormous, you say? How large, then? Larger than the gaping void in our lives?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why, you've even put a smile on Goatie and Croco's faces. All this activity is making for quite the special day.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Pfft. Hahahahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I know that laugh... Liloupar!? What on earth are you doing here!?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Oh, this is hilarious. Turns out good things really do come to those who wait — as long as you stay alive long enough!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: When did you three get locked up in here? And still you act all high and mighty, putting on a show for the younglings... Truly hysterical!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why you...!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Yes, yes... I know, no need to shout... You're right, Liloupar. Goatie, Croco, and I all have the same problem.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: But didn't King Deshret seal you away? How did you break free? And how did you get in here?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Who knows? Perhaps you can ask my master one day, should you ever get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Behold the executioners of old. Some have turned into fragments residing in human bodies, and others are imprisoned eternally, leaving not a single shard behind.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It's almost tragic, watching lowly prisoners like you act all self-important. Curiosity gnaws at you, doesn't it? Your interest in the outside world threatens to burst you at the seams.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm starting to take a liking to this magic bottle lady.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Ahem... Time is of the essence. Let's get down to business.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: We come to you, O three ancient lords, to request your assistance on behalf of the Akademiya. If we can help you regain your freedom, then please consider lending us your aid.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: As for precisely what we need your help with... it's a long story. So, to demonstrate our sincerity, we are prepared to first resolve the problems that plague the three of you.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, stop arguing, Croco. And Goatie, don't you start... What's the harm in letting her speak? It's not worth getting so angry about. Forget about her, the three questions are the crucial thing here.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: But do you really have a way to answer them? You once answered the final question, Nefer, but the seal did not open.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Unless, with the passage of time... you have found a new answer?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You could say so. When you first asked me what determines truth and falsehood, my answer was "a liar's soul."

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Liars are the best at seeing through the falsehoods of the world, but if you want them to tell you the truth, you have to reach their soul.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I think that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: I found it quite compelling myself, and I told Nefer so. Unfortunately, it brought us no closer to liberation.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, that's simply because it was my answer. Not the one that King Deshret was looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Can you guess which answer Al-Ahmar wanted, then?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ..."Time."

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And that's not only the answer to the final question. It's the answer to all three of them.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: All things wax and wane with the passage of time. Love and hate eventually fade into nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Current affairs are always fraught with conflict and controversy. Only time can distinguish between right and wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You once described King Deshret as a proud man. I'd say that the prouder someone is, the more inclined they are to believe that only time is qualified to be their judge.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Time... time... Well, well.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Indeed... Perhaps, in building Aaru, our King was in fact attempting to reverse time... to bring love and hate, right and wrong, the rise and fall of all things back to their point of origin...

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: ...Whew.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: This is the most eventful day I have experienced in a long, long time. You have my sincere gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Are those three of the Seven Pillars?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Turns out the statues were quite faithful to the source.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You three seem to be in good spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Prison can help a person grow and learn to cherish what they have. Nevertheless, after everything you've done for me, I sincerely hope you never have to experience it for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hello, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's good to see you, Thoth the Ibis King.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Nice, nice, nice. Definitely puts my mind at ease, seeing you two getting along so well.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Should we maybe introduce ourselves, or...?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Sure, sure, sure. I'm Sethos, the current leader of the Temple of Silence. This is General Mahamatra Cyno, and this is the former Spantamad Sage Cyrus. But I'm guessing none of that means a whole lot to you?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Everything is equally new to us, in truth. We've been gone from this mortal world for longer than you can imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Let's hold off on the introductions for now. We can always ask Nefer about you later — it'll give me something to talk about with my chosen disciple.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Hah, you're like a helpless parent.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Gods and people of yore are not necessarily welcome in today's world. Self-awareness is one of my finest qualities — I thought I ought to share its fruits with you two.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, I think we'll take it in stride — just as we did with the three questions. Let's not forget, it was my persistence that won you both your freedom!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Fair point. I have to applaud your persistence.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: And I must praise you for your wisdom. Now, state your wishes, young ones.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why, your tremendous accomplishments deserve a reward, do they not? You must let us do something for you in return.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra, what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I won't beat around the bush. Sumeru is facing a crisis the likes of which have never been seen before, and we need your help.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno and Naphis recount the various incidents that have transpired in Sumeru recently...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Every calamity throughout the ages has been connected to us in one way or another, whether we were its cause or consequence.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Whatever is wrong with Irminsul, it severely affected the Dendro Archon. She fell into a coma, and is currently receiving treatment from the Dendro Dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: The Dendro Dragon? I'm sorry... the Dendro Dragon... is helping to heal the Dendro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Not Apep, surely? Not vicious, cruel Apep who possesses no virtues aside from her basic instincts? Ah, good heavens...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I shudder to think what could have caused Lesser Lord Kusanali to suffer such a plight... Still, why would the Dendro Dragon lend you her aid? She has always held nothing but contempt for the archons... I suppose she and Kusanali must have some history. Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: You can help us make history, too.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hahahaha, a smooth talker! Well said, lad.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Currently, no one can connect to Irminsul. We hope that by opening up Aaru and making some modifications to it, we can use its technology to our advantage.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: ...Unfortunately, Aaru is an imperfect creation. King Deshret never managed to realize his full vision before his death. Much remains to be done if it is to be pitted against Irminsul itself.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Besides, I hear your reasons, but to give Aaru up over such would be...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: The archaeological records, clearly indicate that although Aaru's construction took a long time, it was not beyond human means to achieve. Modern technology should solve the efficiency issues... We have no choice but to go all in on this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is by no means a threat, but the only reason we helped you escape from Aaru was to gain the necessary leverage to negotiate with you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You asked us to state our wishes — and we have. Each one of us here needs your help, as do all the thousands of people living in Sumeru. They need you, and they need Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What do we think, my fellow old fogeys? Shall we lend our support, or not?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Since you ask so nicely... naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: ...Naturally what? Are you for or against?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I simply mean we shall do what comes naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: You claim that you wish to open Aaru. Know you, then, that the Golden Slumber created by King Deshret is preserved within?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We do. We understand the risks involved.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: In all likelihood, the mortal world will never again be able to replicate King Deshret's work. Never will there be another chance to come so close to creating a utopia... Knowing this, are you sure of your decision?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We are sure. Before people can dream, they must first live.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: If your minds are made up... Very well. We shall summon our erstwhile colleagues to discuss this further.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Saint Shesepankh, Saint Bennu, once you surrendered to silence and were buried with King Deshret... But now, we invoke the right to awaken you with our voices.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I can feel this... strange sensation. The ground is trembling... as if answering the call of the Goat King.)

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Saint Bennu, responding to your call. Three Kings detected, initiating autonomous will...

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Saint Shesepankh, responding to your call. Three Kings detected, initiating autonomous will...

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Ah, Lord Heryshaf, what a long time it has been. I trust you are keeping well?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Then your trust in my wellbeing has long outlived your physical body. You have always opened with that same phrase, in life, death, and now even beyond.

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Al-Ahmar is long gone. What is the reason for this meeting?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You're awake? Good. We are voting on whether to give the people of present-day Sumeru access to Aaru and permit them to perform technological renovations. You have the right to support or oppose the motion.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Aaru is the pride of Al-Ahmar... Opening Aaru requires the unanimous consent of the Seven Pillars. I hope you have a convincing reason to present to us.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Sumeru is currently in the midst of a major calamity. Let us not forget that while Al-Ahmar was a stern ruler, he was also a teacher of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: A god without his people shall cease to exist, and King Deshret's greatest wish was to provide protection for his people. Let us then honor our God King's wishes as we consider our decision.

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: I do not mean to mock these proceedings, but what is the point of a "unanimous vote" when we know that the last of the Seven Pillars, the Dendro Dragon Apep, will never communicate with us?

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: This will no doubt surprise your mechanical mind, and I have no intention of trying to persuade you it is true... but Apep is, in fact, healing the Dendro Archon as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Can someone attest to this? Do we have any proof?

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: I ask the Three Kings, can any of you vouch for the truth of this claim?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally, the Ibis King, Thoth.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: It was Thoth's disciples who revealed the truth to us. We need not debate its veracity — simply let Thoth bear accountability. That way, the rest of us may have a clear conscience.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Heryshaf, you diabolical fiend!

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I awakened our former colleagues for you, supported your opinion, and backed your decision. What sort of fiend would do that?

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: I miss the days when Hermanubis was still around... At times like this, he would offer to take accountability.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: What are you trying to say? Is my word worth less to you than Hermanubis's?

dialogues.speaker: Shesepankh
dialogues.text: Hypocrite though you are, Lord Thoth, you are humorous in equal measure. How could we bear not to associate with a character such as you? I, Saint Shesepankh, approve the Goat King's proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: ...Since King Deshret is no more, we shall receive no reprimand for acting beyond our remit. Nevertheless, I sincerely hope that those before us understand the significance of what they intend to do.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: Remember: The moment that Aaru is liberated, the myriad souls residing within the Golden Slumber will return to the Ley Lines. And once the Ley Lines flow again, these souls shall in turn be received by Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: To take this step is to bring the perfect afterlife created by our King to a permanent end.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We understand that well, and we have decided to proceed regardless. Furthermore... the contemporary human perspective would contend that confining souls in this way is no act of benevolence. The deceased have a right to rest in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Bennu
dialogues.text: King Deshret's creation is clearly a place of rest and peace, it is just that many do not see it this way... Hmph, but no matter. Saint Bennu approves.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Hermanubis's representative and the Dendro Dragon Apep made their choice ahead of time, while the Goat King, Ibis King, and Crocodile King have also granted permission to liberate Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: By the grace of His Majesty, guided by his wisdom and will... Let the gates of Aaru be reopened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Look at that!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What's this? Are we under attack?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: No, wait... it's...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (These look like souls... Silhouettes approach us from within the light, then pass through our bodies like wind through a veil.)
Here you are... Through the sands of time... I see you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father...? Father, is it really you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Jeht's father, Jebrael! That's right, he entered the Golden Slumber, didn't he...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I smell blood and sand on you... You've grown. Strong as a wild beast, and without shedding a tear.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You... You have to leave, don't you? Please... just answer me this: What... What should I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: This meeting is a blessing from the gods... My soul, once imprisoned along with that of Samail, is finally free. I am truly grateful for the chance to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: That the dead should meet the living is itself a miracle... One brief, precious moment is enough. Enough to set my heart at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Do not weep for me, Jeht. I know you will accomplish many great things in your life. You will go further and climb higher than I ever did. All I ask is that... you take good care of yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father! Father!!!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...Father...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Jeht... Um, do you want something to eat? Maybe it'll help you feel better...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I'm fine. Thanks, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It was just a little sudden... The chance to see my father again meant the world to me.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: He was trapped in the Golden Slumber for our sake, and now, after all this time, he can finally rest in peace... I'm glad. It's a huge relief.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've grown strong, Jeht. More than enough to fend for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah... I'll leave the past in my memory, where it belongs. My family, the good times, and the bad.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Goodbye, Father.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah, me. What a touching reunion that was. It seems we did a good deed today.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: We three retainers, once imprisoned for our iniquity, are surely the least qualified to judge whether this deed is good or bad... Either way, Aaru is open. Now, you have your opportunity — and with it, whatever trouble may ensue.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: Although Aaru was created by a god, human craftsmanship was nevertheless required to build the gate that connects it to this world. Perhaps the relationship between gods and humanity follows a similar principle.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: As for your proposed renovations, we cannot determine which functions to keep or discard. Proceed as you see fit — but please entrust the task to your most accomplished scholars, or Bennu will be most displeased.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: It matters not. The Ibis King shall be accountable if any problems arise. Ibis, you chose to take on disciples, and so it follows that you must accept the risks of associating with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: If I'd known you'd be like this, I would've locked all of you away in Aaru, never to leave again for all eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Sobek
dialogues.text: All of us? What does this have to do with me?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Vilify me no further. Scholars, since you have liberated Aaru, allow me to present you with a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Using Aaru's power, we shall install a defense mechanism at our King's Mausoleum. You must be guarded even against Irminsul itself — this shall afford you some convenience.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: "Unseen, and unheard." From this moment forth, none may by sight or hearing perceive anything said or done within the Mausoleum.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Amazing... And all this is achieved just with the power of Aaru?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: With technology from the heavens, the possibilities are endless. Just because King Deshret did not use it for this purpose does not mean that it cannot be done. So marvel away — this is the reward you have earned.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Alright, well that resolves the issue of confidentiality. What about the technical side? Do we have the manpower?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Why, yes. I've already contacted them. They'll be here soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey everyone, we— Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ah, we meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're... Are you... Thoth, the Ibis King?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: You have a good memory. And unless my eyes deceive me... Hehehe. It appears the young lady next to you has quite the story to tell.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Welcome. Or perhaps, it is you who have welcomed us.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kalu! Kalu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What's wrong? You look a little depressed.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei got a fragment of the Goddess of Flowers, and all I got was one of the Seven Pillars who served under King Deshret... I lost out, didn't I?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...That's what you're upset about? You're such a child.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Paimon! Thanks again for your notes. I'm done copying them, so here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're welcome! Just let Paimon know if you ever need help again.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Good to finally meet you in the flesh.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It's a little surreal seeing you here after exchanging letters for so long. In my head, the Boss of the Curatorium of Secrets didn't look so young.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sounds like you have some history, then?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Any budding mercenary group needs a steady supply of intel. They, in turn, can prove an exceptional source of the same.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The Curatorium of Secrets is happy to cooperate with friends from all over the world. If you're interested, you'd be very welcome to join our network too, Miss Dehya.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Can't say no to a solid partnership, especially out here in the desert. Having intel can mean the difference between life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: But cooperation's built on mutual trust, and there isn't much contact between the desert and Nod-Krai... So, I'm guessing you reached out to Jeht first, Miss Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: What's behind your interest in the desert? Nostalgia? Or is there someone you're looking to take care of...? Let's put all our cards on the table first. Things'll go more smoothly that way.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I like your style, "Flame-Mane." Actually, I had this same discussion with Jeht before we started working together. To be clear, I have no intention of using you for any ulterior motives, and I have no enemies in the desert as things stand now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Were that to change, I wouldn't drag outsiders into a conflict that doesn't concern them. There's no point in doing... certain things, if you don't do them yourself. Wouldn't you agree?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well said. Taking responsibility for one's own affairs is the way of the Desertfolk. Heh, it's like you're one of us.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Uh... You sure that's a compliment?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Absolutely.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'll take it. Hmm... perhaps we can discuss our cooperation in more detail now?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Sure. I love working with no-nonsense people, and you certainly fit that description. I look forward to a fruitful partnership.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: As do I, my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: So many books... More than I could ever read in my life...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: But I've learned a lot that the textbooks could never teach me. I never realized that people in the distant past thought about some of the same questions we ponder today...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The storms have stopped. We should be able to get to the Temple of Silence without any problems now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Time to regroup!

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: I hope everyone's ready. We'll be arriving at our destination very shortly.
